classification.difficultyReason: Convert the region ratio into a fraction of the rectangle's area, identify the trapezium's parallel sides and solve its area equation for x.

content.prompt: A straight line cuts the rectangle below into two trapezia whose areas are in the ratio $3:5$. Find the value of $x$.

spec.description: Rectangle with a sloping divider, top-left segment x m, height 1 m, and two bottom segments each 1 m. Source blue fill is omitted under the unshaded house convention.
spec.mathematics: The two trapezia have parallel side lengths x and 1, and 2-x and 1, respectively, with common height 1. Diagram positions are schematic and supply no additional numerical given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied labels are visible; the value of x is withheld.

answer.short:
$x=\frac12\text{ m}$.

The left trapezium has $\frac38$ of the rectangle's area.
answer.worked:
The rectangle has area $2\times1=2\text{ m}^2$. The left trapezium is the smaller region, so its area is $\frac38\times2=\frac34\text{ m}^2$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{(x+1)\times1}{2}&=\frac34\\x+1&=\frac32\\x&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
Thus $x=\frac12\text{ m}$.
